title: Build one complete customer workflow
outcome: Deliver an inspectable working slice across interface, service, data, and AI.
story: Amina can now explain the first release: staff sign in, search current policies, get a cited draft, review it, and record the outcome. Build that whole path before adding more features.

values.label: path
values.value: form → session check → retrieval → answer → review

frames.explanation: A vertical slice proves connected parts, not just separate demos.
Architecture includes what happens when a dependency fails.

sections.title: Draw the smallest complete system
paragraphs: Show the browser, API, session store, database, policy index, provider adapter, and diagnostic events. Mark where identity is verified, data is filtered, model output is validated, and writes require approval.

Explain each boundary with an input, output, and failure. Keep secrets on the server. The browser should receive only permitted data and public configuration. A diagram is useful when it predicts actual requests rather than merely lists technology names.

sections.title: Build a vertical slice
paragraphs: A vertical slice follows one customer action through all required layers. Start with sign-in, a policy question, scoped retrieval, a cited answer, and human review. Use an offline adapter first and label it clearly.

The downloadable workspace includes a runnable reference slice and extension tasks. Use it to understand boundaries, then complete an independent change. Copying a reference is practice evidence, not independent ownership of the system.

sections.title: Order dependencies and test failures
paragraphs: Data and contracts need to exist before clients depend on them. The lab topologically orders a dependency graph and rejects missing parts or cycles. This is a build-planning rule, not a deployment tool.

The real project tests disconnected and invalid paths: expired session, unavailable provider, missing policy, rejected approval, and duplicate retry. Capture expected/actual outcomes at each boundary and repair the earliest failing boundary.

sections.title: Keep the design understandable
paragraphs: Write short decision records for important choices such as same-origin serving, SQLite, adapter mode, and human approval. Describe the constraint, considered options, choice, and consequence. Prefer a system a teammate can operate and debug.
Keep a runnable main branch and focused reviewable changes. Connect the architecture diagram, API contract, data schema, evaluation report, and release runbook to the actual files and commands.

words.meaning: One complete customer operation working across every needed layer.
A part another part needs in order to work.
A short explanation of a technical choice and its consequences.

example.code:
function buildOrder(parts){const done=new Set();const active=new Set();const result=[];function visit(name){if(done.has(name))return;if(!Object.hasOwn(parts,name))throw new Error("Missing dependency: "+name);if(active.has(name))throw new Error("Cycle: "+name);active.add(name);for(const dependency of parts[name])visit(dependency);active.delete(name);done.add(name);result.push(name);}for(const name of Object.keys(parts))visit(name);return result;}
console.log(buildOrder({ui:["api"],api:["db"],db:[]}));
explanation: The database is visited before its API dependent.
Each completed part is included once.
Missing dependencies and cycles stop the planner.

exercise.title: A dependency-aware build plan
exercise.brief: Write buildOrder(parts), where keys are components and values list their dependencies. Visit keys in insertion order and each dependency in listed order. Return dependencies before dependents. Reject cycles or missing names with Error.

steps.title: List independent parts
steps.task: Return keys in their given order for graphs with no dependencies.
steps.hint: Object.keys keeps the supplied key order.

steps.title: Visit dependencies first
steps.task: Use a depth-first visit and include each completed part once.
steps.hint: Visit a part’s dependencies before pushing its name.
steps.solution: function buildOrder(parts){const done=new Set();const result=[];function visit(name){if(done.has(name))return;for(const dependency of parts[name])visit(dependency);done.add(name);result.push(name);}for(const name of Object.keys(parts))visit(name);return result;}

steps.title: Reject impossible plans
steps.task: Track active visits to detect cycles; reject names absent from parts.
steps.hint: A visiting set differs from a completed set.
steps.solution: function buildOrder(parts){const done=new Set();const active=new Set();const result=[];function visit(name){if(done.has(name))return;if(!Object.hasOwn(parts,name))throw new Error("Missing dependency: "+name);if(active.has(name))throw new Error("Cycle: "+name);active.add(name);for(const dependency of parts[name])visit(dependency);active.delete(name);done.add(name);result.push(name);}for(const name of Object.keys(parts))visit(name);return result;}

cases.label: No components
cases.why: An empty plan has no work.

cases.label: A shared dependency
cases.why: A shared part appears only once.

cases.label: A cyclic graph
cases.why: A cycle cannot satisfy this build plan.

cases.why: Missing parts need a deliberate repair.

project.title: Amina’s complete policy-assistant capstone
project.brief: Use the workspace to deliver the customer-reviewed slice. Implement an independent feature and demonstrate both normal and denied/failing paths.
deliverables: An integrated test and AI evaluation report.

milestones.title: Run and understand
actions: Trace one request across the actual files.

milestones.title: Own a complete change
actions: Choose a requirement from the reviewed brief.
Implement it across the necessary boundaries.
Add meaningful tests and document the decision.

milestones.title: Demonstrate the result
actions: Show sign-in, scoped retrieval, citations, and review.
Reproduce provider, permission, and missing-source failures.
Ask a reviewer to run the project from the README.

acceptance: The whole main flow runs from documented commands.
Permissions apply before data reaches the model.
An independent change has tests and reviewer evidence.

tests.situation: Another shop session asks the question

tests.expected: The interface shows the defined fallback.
The main flow and tests are reproducible.

project.extension: Add a second customer workflow and explain how it changes the architecture and evaluation requirements.
